title: Provisional owner matrix and micro-econ scratchpad (May 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight scratchpad to map provisional owners for the upcoming weekend surge window, approximate incremental cost exposure using a simple token-hour proxy, and capture quick handoff notes for cross-functional liaisons. Not a canonical source of truth — use for quick coordination and triage only.

Context / why this exists:
- We expect a short, high-variance traffic spike on 2026-05-22 (marketing experiment + external partner test).
- Need provisional people mapped to responsibilities (routing, model fallback, billing flags, customer comms) so weekend on-call can cover without deep pre-planning.
- Finance asked for a quick ballpark of incremental run-rate for the spike to decide on temporary burst credits.

High-level assumptions used for micro-econ proxy:
- Baseline throughput: 2.3M tokens/day across hosted API routes relevant to the experiment.
- Spike multiplier: 4x for 24 hours (peak window), then 1.5x for next 48 hours.
- Unit cost proxy: $0.000012 per token (quick blended rate across models + embeddings used in sample).
- Ops overhead fudge factor: +12% to cover transient autoscale and on-call labor.

Quick calc (rounded):
- Baseline tokens/day: 2,300,000 -> baseline daily cost = 2,300,000 * 0.000012 = $27.6
- Peak day tokens (4x): 9,200,000 -> peak cost = $110.4
- Next two days at 1.5x: each 3,450,000 -> each day cost = $41.4 -> two days = $82.8
- 3-day incremental cost over baseline (peak+2days - 3*baseline): (110.4+82.8) - (27.6*3) = 193.2 - 82.8 = $110.4
- +12% ops overhead = $110.4 * 1.12 = ~$123.6 -> round to $125 as request to finance for emergency burst credits.

Provisional owner matrix (single line per responsibility — minimize back-and-forth):
- Routing & failover (model variant policy / region fallback): Jon Park (eng-platform-engineering)
- Autoscale / capacity knobs (burst config & throttles): Priya N. (infra) -- reachable via #infra-oncall
- Cost gating / emergency budget toggle: Sofia Alvarez (finance lead)
- Customer communications / partner liaison: Ethan Lee (solutions-eng)
- Console telemetry + dashboard quick filters: Aria Patel (product-ops)
- Post-mortem + eval prompt set capture: Miro Chen (applied-ml)

Open questions / quick TODOs (sorted by priority):
1) Confirm token blending methodology with billing team (Sofia) — do we include embeddings run for search re-rank? (high)
2) Validate that Dedicated pools are not impacted by this hosted spike (Priya) — if yes, update routing policy to divert to Dedicated for enterprise routes. (high)
3) Create a one-click dashboard filter for "experiment-X / partner-Y" traffic in Console so on-call can triage quickly (Aria -> finish by EOD 05/20). (med)
4) Define automatic fallback model variant sequence for >200ms tail latency events (Jon -> produce a short policy). (med)
5) Post-event evaluation: capture 20 sample prompts flagged by partner for offline quality check (Miro -> assign prompt set). (low)

Notes to self / scratch bits:
- If finance pushes back, propose a $125 emergency credit for the 3-day window (rounded number, include buffer).
- Consider temporary client-side rate limit for the partner if runtime cost > threshold (discuss with SE).
- Keep response streaming enabled — partner is sensitive to latency > bad UX.

Mini-runbook (one-paragraph):
At spike detection or experiment start, routing lead (Jon) switches experimental route to burst policy A (allows 4x for 1h then decays). Infra lead (Priya) verifies Dedicated pools are isolated; if not, enable transient divert rule. Finance (Sofia) pre-approves $125 credit to cover incremental token spend. Solutions Eng (Ethan) posts a short status note to partner channel and sets expectation for 24-72h monitoring. Product Ops (Aria) watches console dashboard and triggers model fallback if error rates exceed 1% or 95th latency > 400ms for >5 minutes. After window, collect logs, sample prompts, and schedule a 30-min postmortem the following Tue.

Metrics to capture during window (minimum):
- total tokens per route (1-min granularity)
- p95 and p99 latency per model variant
- model error rate (% non-200 or failed decodes)
- cost per token rolling sum (1h)
- number of fallback activations

Quick audit checklist (post-window):
- [ ] Confirm actual incremental tokens and reconcile with proxy
- [ ] Confirm Dedicated isolation (infra note)
- [ ] Capture 20 sample prompts for quality eval and flag regressions
- [ ] Publish short incident note to #ops-summary and tag SE/Finance
- [ ] Close the temporary budget request or convert to formal AR if needed

Final quick thoughts (informal):
This is intentionally sparse — the goal is speed over precision. If anything here changes, update the owner matrix and ping the on-call channel. I'll drop a short Loom later with the dashboard filters.

Recent edits log (brief):
